steps.content: You and Nolaine rush toward Hilda at the same instant.

A violent explosion roars behind you. The shockwave, thick with Mania, slams into you, hurling everyone forward like ragdolls. The world dissolves into a cacophony of shattering sounds. You can't even tell if it's the building breaking apart or the snap of human bones.
(Black screen for 5+ seconds) (Dim light + debris sounds)
An unknown amount of time passes. You open your eyes to utter darkness.
A high-pitched ring is the only sound in your ears. Then, a deep, bone-jarring ache registers, radiating from the heavy weight pinning your legs and torso.

You try to move. A sharp pain flares, but your limbs respond. A collapsed sofa and chairs lie across you, but they've wedged against fallen ceiling panels, forming a fragile, triangular pocket of space around you.
Miraculously, nothing seems broken. Gritting your teeth, you carefully push aside chunks of plaster and splintered wood, slowly dragging your body out from under the wreckage.
Your palms press into the ground—and meet a warm, sticky wetness. You try not to think about what it is.
The air is thick with chalky dust and a heavy, cloying concentration of raw Mania. You try to take a steadying breath, but the moment you open your mouth, an uncontrollable cough wracks your body.
After a moment, you hear a sound coming from nearby.
${PlayerName}?
Hilda's Trust +1

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You're alright. That's a relief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How are you? What about Nolaine, Manphist, and Helene?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Manphist... is gone. Helene was clear of the blast radius. She should be fine.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: As for Nolaine, she...
You hear a faint groaning from the shadows to your left. Rubble shifts and crumbles as you discover Nolaine, trapped between two fallen support beams.
She was closest to Manphist and took the full force of the explosion to protect Hilda. Half her body is mangled beyond recognition, replaced by twisted limbs that writhe with spreading Mania.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: ...Quite fitting, isn't it?
She coughs. It's a wet, gurgling sound, the noise of bloody foam churning in her throat.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: You always shut me out... Hilda. Pushed me away. No matter how many of your codes I broke, you never let me in... never let me join you.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I thought you were looking down on me. So I went to Manphist...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: He said I had talent... that he appreciated my skills... He wrote the recommendation... got me into the Cryptography Department...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I never realized he was just using me to get to you... I was so naive, thinking it was my own skill... that let me fight my way to your side...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I... I really wanted to go to Sevael.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I can't remember a single good day from my childhood... My stomach was always a hollow ache... even with one meal, I was terrified of where the next would come from... gunfire could erupt in the alleyways at any moment...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: When I thought life was meaningless... you were the one who saved me. You showed me a city-state could be something more...
[Flashback Filter] [Alley Corner]

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I knew you weren't ordinary... The kind lady who always slips me an extra half-slice of black bread at the relief station is actually a high-value Outland agent.
The little beggar tossed a wallet playfully between her hands, its ID cards and notes fluttering with each movement.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You're more observant than I gave you credit for.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: So, clever girl, what's the price for your silence? A basket of bread? Or... do you plan to sell me out to those hyenas waiting for their reward at the end of the alley?

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Bread? How long would that last me? And selling you out? Those hyenas would silence me right after. I'm not stupid.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I've been watching you. The way you walk, the way you observe people... it's different from the real charity workers. You avoid patrols with a skill even sharper than us street rats.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: And sometimes... there's a scent on you. Not perfume. Chemicals and fire. It's faint, but I can smell it.
Her small face was flushed red, whether from frostbite or excitement, it was impossible to tell. It gave her a fierceness well beyond her years.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I don't want bread, and I don't want your life. I want... to go with you. I want to learn your skills.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: This world has no good or evil, no justice, only power...! I want what you have. I want them to fear me. I want to be able to change things...!

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...No. There is good and evil in this world. There is justice.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You're still a child. I hope you can hold on to that belief.
She crouched down, bringing herself to eye level with the young girl.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I'm from a city-state that was once filled with light and governed by justice. I came to DisCity to help it become the same.
[Fade to black for storytelling]
This is a crossroads for the world. In its street-side cafes, people peruse newspapers in dozens of languages, eagerly trading phrases from their homelands.
All children attend school; everyone has work and receives their rightful share. Theaters constantly debut new plays, and a laundry woman can walk proudly into a masquerade to dance with nobility.
No wars, no conflicts. People of every rank fulfill their duties, yet still have the energy to enjoy their lives.
Back then, it was the clearest vision of an ideal, an indestructible lighthouse in the hearts of countless souls.
[End Flashback Filter]

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Though war has scarred our world, I still believe that if we stand together, we can reclaim the shared ideals we once held.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Give that back to me now, child. I won't bring you into our work, but I can give you all the money I have and take you somewhere safe and warm.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You belong in a classroom, not on a battlefield...
[End of Flashback]

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Of course... in the end... you couldn't talk me out of it...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: But even now... I'm still not sure that I made the wrong choice.
Her voice breaks, fracturing into pieces, but her gaze holds Hilda's, fierce and unyielding.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: You once told me... you became a spy... because you wanted the city-state to become that ideal in your heart. That kind of city-state... must have truly existed once, right?

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I don't understand... When I work undercover, when I'm used by others... am I doing something wrong, or... something good? I really... can't tell anymore.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: But as long as we're moving towards the right goal, we won't lose our way... right?

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Hilda, you're different from me. You're smarter. You can definitely stay on the right path... because you... never lose sight of the goal.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: What we're facing now... is just an inevitable obstacle on the path... that's all. We'll overcome it eventually... right?

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: ...And now you even have this special power. One that can see through everything and show the way forward... right?
Nolaine's breaths grow fainter, dwindling to a whisper.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Then can you tell me... which path is truly the right one?
The girl's last word hangs in the air and vanishes. Yet her eyes stay open, lingering on yours, waiting for an answer.
A long, heavy silence settles between you.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Don't follow my example. Even with this power... there are still many things I cannot see through.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: In the end... haven't I lost you too?
But Hilda will never again hear a response from Nolaine.
Her figure is swallowed by the darkness. With Nolaine's death, Hilda's cold, hard shell seems to collapse, and she sinks into a deathly silence.
No response. Only the sound of heavy breathing, as if she had melted completely into the shadows.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This isn't your fault. Nolaine died in Manphist's suicide attack. You had nothing to do with it.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...No. This is my fault.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I... was the one who told her Sevael's story... filling her head with unrealistic fantasies about the metropoles.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I... was also the one who failed to stop her from joining us, who didn't guide her properly, letting her be used by Manphist and make terrible mistakes.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: With hollow ideals and beliefs, I led an innocent person astray... I took the life she should have lived...!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Hilda.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Having ideals isn't wrong. What's wrong are those cowards who manipulate others like pawns from the shadows, sending them into battle while profiting from their sacrifice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Johnson sat in his position of power in the metropoles, yet he was nothing but scum who manipulated power and wealth without any morality; Manphist was a despised opportunist who'd turn at the slightest breeze, yet the metropoles welcomed him with open arms and generous rewards.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And then there's the hardest truth to accept: their exploitation of satellite towns, even dropping nuclear bombs on civilians to crush DisCity's rebellion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They wave the banner of human unity while ruthlessly exploiting border regions and small states, using grand ideals as bait to make countless aspirational people sacrifice themselves for their cause.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Now that we've seen the truth... are you willing to keep being their pawn and continue down this path?
You hear a faint, dry sound in the air, like the friction of her knuckles tightening into a fist.
The silence that follows is broken only by the strain of her suppressed breath. It lasts for a long moment before she finally finds her voice.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Is there any other way?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes. As long as we survive and get this evidence out, we can expose what we've witnessed and show the true face of the metropoles to more people. Even just a fragment of truth is enough to keep certain people awake at night!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course, if we end up like your parents, hunted by the metropoles, or completely erased...
Drawing a deep breath, you finally give voice to the dangerous, inciting thought you've harbored for so long.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then let's go to DisCity... to the farlands... to places willing to hear the truth, willing to fight against exploitation and oppression, where we can truly realize our ideals of what a city-state should be.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A metropole like this doesn't deserve our loyalty.
A few days ago, these words for Hilda would have been unthinkable. Now, it doesn't matter anymore.

The mole is gone, the Monolith a phantom, the spy a lie. All that remains is a fool, toyed with and betrayed by the homeland she trusted so deeply. Now she is just a soul adrift, bewildered and utterly lost.
Silence stretches in the dark. When her answer finally comes, it's not the one you want.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...I don't think I can anymore...
A wave of dread washes over you. You immediately reach out, groping through the oppressive darkness toward the sound of her voice.
Your fingers find something wet first. Then, a hand rises to carefully touch your cheek. You seize it firmly in your own.
From the darkness, Hilda lets out a wry, pained laugh.
Her gloves are in tatters, shredded by the violent emergence of Mania spikes, revealing the torn and bleeding skin beneath.

This outbreak is far more severe than the last; the spikes are denser, more aggressive. Given the immense power she just unleashed against Manphist, the backlash from overexertion must be excruciating.
Right now, the shackles are the only option left.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can try using another power to neutralize your contamination. No guarantees it'll work, but... are you willing to let me try?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You're really an anomalous power expert?
"I really am. I just can't use my power because your LINK consciousness has been rejecting me," you grumble to yourself inwardly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can only try.
You've tried this before. The shackles had no effect on her then, but now...
A faint red light shimmers into existence in your hand as you cautiously reach for hers.
This time, there's no violent resistance. A small portion of the shackle's energy absorbs into her palm, but most of it simply flickers and dissolves into the air.
Yet, it's enough. The chaotic turmoil raging within her body begins to gradually subside.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Thank you.
The flickering shackles cast a faint glow through the cramped space, illuminating Hilda's form nearby.
[Wounded CG]
She is closer than you imagined. Her head hangs low, hair veiling her features.
Sharp, solidified strands of Mania have pierced clean through her body, transforming her into a living pillar that desperately holds up the collapsed rubble.
She is the only reason this triangular safe zone exists. The space that protects you is the space her body buys.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...So you... saw it.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Don't worry, it looks worse than it is... As long as one of us made it out... that's enough...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Trust me, I'm getting us both out of here.

steps.content: You immediately use the light to examine the collapsed surroundings.

Before the explosion, you were in the interrogation room beneath the manor. From what you can see now, the first floor directly above has completely collapsed. Escaping straight up is impossible, but...
You remember the manor's documents, the map of secret passages. A tunnel extends from this very chamber.
The switch is hidden behind the storage cabinet against the wall. You desperately try to recall everyone's positions in the moment before the blast.

Manphist was lunging toward the interrogation table when the explosion erupted from that point. Nolaine was closest to it, you were next, and Hilda was furthest away. And if your current positions—yours, Hilda's, and Nolaine's—were rearranged by the blast's force...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There!
Just a meter or two behind Hilda lies the entrance to the secret passage, blocked only by a few loose rocks.
When you tell her about the secret passage, Hilda's eyes widen in surprise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Look, even your parents are still watching over you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't give up, Hilda. I'm not giving up either.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Okay.
She nods resolutely, and you immediately spring into action.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm going to try to move these rocks. It might hurt, so bear with me.
You start by clearing the smaller, movable rocks from around Hilda, working to create enough space for both of you to escape.
The stones grind against Hilda's shattered shoulder, forcing a sharp hiss of air through her clenched teeth. Yet her eyes lock with yours, burning with a silent, urgent command to continue.
Crack. An alarming sound splinters the air from the surrounding rubble. In response, Hilda calmly raises her left hand.
Those Mania strips spiral from her body once more. They whip through the dust-choked air, coiling around the unstable stones like spectral bands of steel. In an instant, the collapse is halted.
A fresh wave of cold sweat glistens on her ashen face.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I never thought that power could be used like this...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hang in there! I'm almost done!
You pull and heave at the stones with all your strength. Each time the rubble shifts and groans, threatening to collapse, Hilda releases a surge of her Mania to lock the falling debris in place.

Time loses all meaning. Your world narrows to the weight of rock and the growing, throbbing pain in your hands. Your fingers are soon raw and bleeding, leaving crimson smears on every stone you manage to drag away.

Then, as you wrestle aside a final, fist-sized rock, you see the dull color of a storage box. The container is half-crushed from the explosion, but what steals your breath lies behind the shattered panel—a dark, yawning opening to a passage.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We've got a way out, Hilda!
[Scene Change: Cellar]
You emerge from the collapsed entrance, both too exhausted to take another step.
Still, your hand finds Hilda's. You press your barely effective shackles against her skin, struggling to calm the rampaging Mania that surges through her.
The wild crackle of Mania slowly fades from her body. In your daze, you think you hear the ghost of her laughter, but it must be your imagination.
Because neither of you has the strength left to speak.
Then, a slight movement in your hand. Her fingers trace a faint, deliberate pattern against your palm, a brief message in code.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You really are... a remarkably kind person.
